heading: ### What stays open — named, never closed by prose

findings.skill_statement: The round-8 `[U]` on a fleet driver invoking the tick with no lane acting is cited at `:1017-1019`, but at C* those lines stop mid-sentence ("... an executed command at") and the `[U]` sentence is at `:1020-1021` ("no lane acting stays [U]."). The range was correct at round 52 (7ff81a5: [U] at line 1019) and broke under round-53's own insertions above it (diff hunk `@@ -922,6 +922,8 @@`, +2 lines), so the anchor no longer resolves to the statement it names.

The cited range no longer carries the six-leg registry ledger-row statement: at C* `:1359-1363` is the "Reading a receipt" bullet, while the named statement ("a ledger row recording the six-leg (ten-leg since round 51) registry is the ledger owner's follow-on") sits at `:1366-1370`. The range was exact at round 52 (7ff81a5: that bullet at 1359-1363) and was shifted by round-53's insertions (hunks `@@ -1246,5 +1248,9 @@` +4, `@@ -1355,5 +1361,6 @@` +1, plus the +2 above).

The registry is named "six-leg" with no date, but at C* it embeds ten legs: `:1363-1364` "the tool embeds ten since round 51", `:1368` "the six-leg (ten-leg since round 51) registry", `:1398` "six-leg registry at round 11, seven since round 16, eight since round 18, nine since round 26, ten since round 51". The page's own round-16 repair table records this identical bare token as a stale count (`| 1391 | "six-leg registry" | six at round 11, seven since round 16 |`), so an undated "six-leg registry" fails the page's own convention.
